correctness.rationale: For each prime exponent at least two, the normalized e-unitary divisor sum is maximized by exponent two at 1+1/p; among exponents three and higher it is at most 1+1/p² with equality only at exponent three, established by exact divisor analysis through exponent six and a convergent tail bound for every exponent at least seven. Sorting core primes then leaves only (2,5,7) and (2,3,r), each resolved by strict rational inequalities; only core values 36,1800,2700 meet ratio two. Singleton exponents contribute ratio one. All parameter boundaries and n=1 are included; checker confirms 500000 initial inputs and 150444 core prime/exponent parameter cases without purporting to prove infinity.

value.rationale: The boundary at three powerful-core primes is intrinsic: two-prime classification was published, 1800 and 2700 are natural three-prime examples, and the underlying paper explicitly asks whether e-unitary perfectness can differ from ordinary e-perfectness. A uniform local excess bound gives a complete natural classification for every exponent and arbitrary squarefree tails and proves that any exotic example needs at least four distinct core primes. The contribution is structural, not a finite-table repetition or an arbitrary numeric cutoff.
